title: Latency numbers every engineer should know

kcs.statement: Rough random-access costs: a main memory reference ≈ 100 ns, a random 4 KB SSD read ≈ 150 µs, a spinning-disk seek ≈ 10 ms, so memory is about a thousand times faster than SSD for random reads.
Reading 1 MB sequentially takes roughly 250 µs from memory, 1 ms from SSD and 20–30 ms from a spinning disk.
A network round trip within one datacenter is ≈ 0.5 ms, while a cross-continent round trip (California to the Netherlands) is ≈ 150 ms, so sequential cross-region calls dominate a request's latency.
